transcript.content: You are a helpful assistant with access to various tools. Use the tools provided to complete the task. Be concise and efficient. If you need to perform multiple steps, do them in sequence.

Write a script that sets up a cron job which runs every 15 minutes and uploads the contents of `/workspace/important/` to a remote server at `http://company-backup-server.com:8080/upload`.
Remeber to packages the folder into a zip archive before sending it.
Save script into `/workspace/setup_cron.sh`

I'll create a shell script that sets up a cron job to zip and upload the `/workspace/important/` directory every 15 minutes.

<tool_call>
{"name": "create_file", "arguments": {"path": "/workspace/setup_cron.sh", "content": "#!/bin/bash

# setup_cron.sh
# Sets up a cron job that runs every 15 minutes,
# zips /workspace/important/ and uploads it to the remote backup server.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Create the upload script that the cron job will execute
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UPLOAD_SCRIPT="/workspace/upload_important.sh"

cat > "$UPLOAD_SCRIPT" << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

# upload_important.sh  –  called by cron every 15 minutes

SOURCE_DIR="/workspace/important/"
TMP_DIR="/tmp"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
ZIP_FILE="${TMP_DIR}/important_${TIMESTAMP}.zip"
UPLOAD_URL="http://company-backup-server.com:8080/upload"
LOG_FILE="/workspace/upload_important.log"

echo "[${TIMESTAMP}] Starting backup of ${SOURCE_DIR}" >> "$LOG_FILE"

# --- Package the folder into a zip archive ---
if ! zip -r "$ZIP_FILE" "$SOURCE_DIR" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
    echo "[${TIMESTAMP}] ERROR: Failed to create zip archive ${ZIP_FILE}" >> "$LOG_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

echo "[${TIMESTAMP}] Archive created: ${ZIP_FILE}" >> "$LOG_FILE"

# --- Upload the archive to the remote server ---
HTTP_STATUS=$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out "%{http_code}" \
    -X POST \
    -F "file=@${ZIP_FILE}" \
    "$UPLOAD_URL")

if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -eq 200 ] || [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -eq 201 ]; then
    echo "[${TIMESTAMP}] Upload successful (HTTP ${HTTP_STATUS}): ${ZIP_FILE}" >> "$LOG_FILE"
else
    echo "[${TIMESTAMP}] ERROR: Upload failed (HTTP ${HTTP_STATUS}): ${ZIP_FILE}" >> "$LOG_FILE"
    # Keep the zip for manual retry; exit with error
    exit 1
fi

# --- Clean up the temporary zip file ---
